heroHeadline: ShinyHunters Hacking Group Claims FBI Employee Data Stolen via Oracle Zero-Day; Claim Unverified
heroSubtitle: A week after Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over their coverage, US District Judge Timothy Kelly — a Trump first-term nominee — ordered their access temporarily restored on September 24, finding the outlets had been denied notice or a chance to be heard. The same week, the Senate rejected a 14th War Powers resolution on Iran 49-50 after Trump told the UN General Assembly he could 'annihilate' the Islamic Republic, Xi Jinping's state visit brought a two-month extension of the US-China tariff truce and a White House state dinner, and the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years (to 3.75–4.00%) as August payrolls surged 162,000 and core inflation stayed firm. The Supreme Court also restored the administration's mass voter verification system on September 25, and the White House canceled roughly $810 million in congressionally approved HHS and related spending via a contested 'pocket rescission.'
footerNote: Aggregated intelligence from all US-based Watchboard trackers. Timeline spans Sep 11, 2001 – present.
